_note: Contract regex-limit v1 (camada-all-2pap): bounded cost of customer `matches` regexes at match time, and the save-time refusal of patterns re2js cannot compile. Byte-identical copies, change all of them together and update the sha256 every suite pins: camada/edge-analyst/test/regex-limit-vectors.json, camada-backend/test/regex-limit-vectors.json, camada-web/src/lib/regex-limit-vectors.json, camada-core/test/fixtures/regex-limit/regex-limit-vectors.json (the server SDKs read this one from the camada-core sibling checkout, like blk5; CAMADA_FIXTURES_DIR overrides). An input value is a string, or {prefix?, repeat, times, suffix?} meaning prefix + repeat x times + suffix. Each row is one rule in snapshot meta form; parse it into a v5 snapshot (camada-core blk5/v5-empty.bin with meta.rules = [rule]) and match the input: hit = the result names the rule. Engine classes: linear = re2js (edge-analyst, camada-core and the JS adapters through it) and Go regexp, which give the true answer; budget = Python regex timeout, Ruby Regexp timeout (3.2+), PHP PCRE match limit, Java deadline CharSequence, .NET matchTimeout, where an over-limit run answers like an over-cap value: hit for block/challenge/warn, miss for skip. over_limit: every engine runs every row and asserts hit[class]. linear_time: linear engines only; hit as given, and a fresh compile plus the first match takes under max_ms (best of 3). refused: patterns re2js refuses (the regex-guard screen accepts most of them; v1.4 below covers the ones it refuses first); edge-analyst validateCond, camada-backend regexError and camada-web regexProblem refuse each with the re2 kind (or the guard text, per v1.4), and, for refused_rule with the pattern as its one condition, every matcher answers cases[].hit[go] in camada-go, edge-analyst and camada-core (and the JS adapters through it), where a pattern Go or re2js refuses never matches (edge-analyst and camada-core since camada-all-rfyr), and hit[native] in the backtracking SDKs, which compile them. accepted: guard- and re2js-accepted patterns no save-time check may refuse. translate: [JS pattern, jsToRe2 output] pairs that the four JS copies (edge-analyst blocklist.js, camada-core path.ts, camada-backend rules-custom.ts, camada-web lib/rules.ts) reproduce exactly with re2js 2.9.0; other languages ignore it. JS without u reads \x not followed by two hex digits as a plain x, and [\b] as a backspace (v1.1, camada-all-2pap review). v1.2: astral surrogate pairs, [\c_]-style class controls, [\B], and - next to a class escape in a class (camada-all-2pap review); rule (d) for that last one was replaced in v1.3 by a refusal (a [\s-z]-style - next to a class escape in a class is refused, never translated). constants: every port asserts its own constant equals the value here. v1.4 (camada-all-mx0h, camada-all-sl00, camada-all-648h): a repeat count written with a leading zero is read as its decimal value, as JS without u reads it. jsToRe2 strips the zeros from each number of an unescaped quantifier brace outside [ ] (a{02} -> a{2}, a{01001} -> a{1001}; [{02}] and \{02} stay as written), and camada-go jsToRE2 reads such a count the same way (pinned for Go by refused RF6 and blk5 LZ1-LZ3, since Go ignores translate). refused also holds patterns the save-time screen refuses before re2js is asked: for such a row (RF5 a{1001} and RF6 a{01001}, both refused first by the camada-all-8r29 repeat-count check) edge-analyst validateCond, camada-backend regexError and camada-web regexProblem answer with the guard's repeat-count text, not the re2 kind, and the row stays in refused because its refused_rule cases pin how a stored pattern saved before that check runs. constants.RE2_DFA_MAX_MEM is the re2js lazy-DFA memory bound per compiled pattern, in bytes (camada-all-sl00); edge-analyst and camada-core assert it and the other ports ignore it, as each port asserts only the constants it has. v1.5 (camada-all-nyy0): accepted drops \u00e9, \Aabc\z and \p{L}: the regex-guard refuses every \u, \A, \z, \p and \P (kind escape), since PHP cannot compile \u and Python cannot compile \z or \p. Their translate rows stay, because stored rules and CVE feed patterns still go through jsToRe2. v1.6 (camada-all-skld): over_limit OL6-OL11 are shapes the regex-guard static screen accepts (its known residuals and its V8 calibration, contracts.md A4): residual A, the 8-level residual B and [0-9]?x12 then (?:a{5}|a{6}|a{7}|a{8}), each as a block row whose input matches and a skip row whose input does not, so every engine class gets the same answer whether or not a budget engine runs out of time (deny hit, skip miss when over); the three patterns are also in accepted. v1.7 (camada-all-4s9z): translate gains x[[:alpha:]]y -> x[\[:alpha:]]y and x[^[:a:]]y -> x[^\[:a:]]y: JS reads a [ inside a class as text, so jsToRe2 writes it as \[ and RE2 never reads [:alpha:] as a POSIX class (camada-all-07c7, camada-all-kdq0); the regex-guard refuses both at save (kind posix), so they are not in accepted. accepted gains x[a-b-\d]y, x[a-z-\w]y and x[\x41-\x5a-\w]y: a - right after a finished class range is a literal, as V8 and RE2 read it (camada-all-uged). v1.8 (camada-all-04la): translate gains x[\S]y -> the JS non-whitespace ranges written out: jsToRe2 expands \S inside [ ] to the code points JS \S matches, since RE2 \S is ASCII-only (camada-all-ao29). translate_refused: JS patterns every jsToRe2 copy refuses with a SyntaxError, never translates (a - next to \s, \d or \w inside [ ], per v1.3; a raw [ inside a class is an atom there, so x[[-\d]y is refused); the four JS suites assert it and other languages ignore it. v1.9 (camada-all-ax9h): accepted_match: x[a-b-\d]y, x[a-z-\w]y and x[\x41-\x5a-\w]y from accepted, run like refused rows (refused_rule with the pattern as its one condition, matched against each case's ua) by every matcher: hit[go] in camada-go, edge-analyst and camada-core (and the JS adapters through it), hit[native] in the backtracking SDKs, each through its own JS translation and engine; the two classes agree on every case. x-y hits because a - right after a finished class range is a literal; the miss rules out a range read through it (xcy for b-d with \d read as d, x^y for \x5a-w), and x.y a class that takes anything. A pattern an engine cannot compile never matches there, so its hit cases fail. camada-backend and camada-web only pin the sha.

over_limit.why: over the limit a deny rule hits although the regex would miss
over the limit a skip rule misses
a skip whose regex truly matches still misses when the limit runs out first
a deny rule hits either way
path regexes run case-insensitively over three path forms; the limit holds there too
regex-guard residual A (camada-all-skld), accepted at save, 272 ms in V8 unbounded: the input matches, so a deny rule hits whether the run finishes or runs out of budget
residual A: the input does not match, so a skip rule misses whether the run finishes or runs out of budget
regex-guard residual B, 8 levels (153 ms V8, 372 ms Python re, unbounded): the input matches, a deny rule hits either way
residual B: the input does not match, a skip rule misses either way (Python regex runs past the 50 ms budget here)
V8-calibrated bar (1.9 ms V8, 330 ms Python re): the input matches, a deny rule hits either way
V8-calibrated bar: the input does not match, a skip rule misses either way

refused.kind: repeat count written with a leading zero

accepted_match.kind: literal - between the range a-b and \d
literal - between the range a-z and \w
